title: Power lifting implies universal submersiveness of an affine invariant quotient
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $H$ an affine finite-type group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$. For a commutative $k$-algebra $D$, a rational $H$-action is a $k$-algebra coaction $\rho_D:D\to D\otimes_k k[H]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities, and $D^H=\{d:\rho_D(d)=d\otimes1\}$. Suppose that for every surjective equivariant homomorphism $D\twoheadrightarrow D'$ of rational $H$-algebras (without finite-generation restrictions) and every $b\in(D')^H$, some positive power of $b$ is the image of an element of $D^H$. Then for every finitely generated rational $H$-algebra $E$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}(E^H)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is universally submersive: for every commutative $E^H$-algebra $L$, the continuous map $\operatorname{Spec}(E\otimes_{E^H}L)\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is surjective and a subset of its target is open if and only if its inverse image is open. The invariant ring is not assumed Noetherian or finitely generated.

proof.text: Fix a finitely generated rational $H$-algebra $E$, and put $R=E^H$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}E$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$. By [lem-sfb-flat-affine-action-stack-presentation], form the quasi-compact, quasi-separated algebraic stack $\mathcal X=[U/H]$, the universally open surjective presentation $\pi:U\to\mathcal X$, and the quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$. The composite $\phi\pi$ is precisely the morphism induced by $R\hookrightarrow E$. This construction applies to non-smooth $H$ as well.

Let $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ be any surjection of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-algebras and let $t\in\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal B)$. By [lem-sfb-flat-affine-action-algebra-descent], it corresponds to a surjective equivariant $E$-algebra map $D\twoheadrightarrow D'$, and $t$ corresponds to $b\in(D')^H$. Forgetting to $k$-algebras preserves both surjectivity and equivariance. The assumed lifting property produces $N>0$ and $a\in D^H$ mapping to $b^N$. Write $\alpha:\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)\cong D^H$ and $\beta:\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal B)\cong(D')^H$ for the natural algebra isomorphisms in the descent theorem. Set $s=\alpha^{-1}(a)$. Naturality gives $\beta(\operatorname{image}(s))=\operatorname{image}(a)=b^N=\beta(t)^N=\beta(t^N)$, so injectivity of $\beta$ gives $\operatorname{image}(s)=t^N$. These algebras need not be finitely generated, exactly as permitted by the hypothesis. For the structure algebra the same theorem identifies $R\to\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})$ with the identity.

source.place: Tag 06WT; Alper Lemma 9.2.5 (3), applied directly to algebras on the affine action quotient

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-global-power-lifting-adequacy] to $\phi:\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$: step 1 supplies quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of both $\mathcal X$ and $\phi$, and step 2 supplies power lifts for every quasi-coherent algebra surjection. Its structure-algebra identification is for the actual ring map induced by $\phi$, so the criterion's global-functions hypothesis holds for this morphism. Consequently $\phi$ is an adequate moduli space. In particular the criterion supplies power lifts for all quasi-coherent algebras on every affine etale base change, including algebras not pulled back from $\mathcal X$; this is the local condition in the current definition. No commutation of invariants with arbitrary scalar extension is asserted.

For any commutative $R$-algebra $L$, set $T=\operatorname{Spec}L$ and $\mathcal X_T=\mathcal X\times_YT$. The theorem [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-universally-submersive] applied to the adequate moduli map just obtained says that $g:|\mathcal X_T|\to|T|$ is surjective and $V\subseteq|T|$ is open exactly when $g^{-1}V$ is open. It applies to this arbitrary $T\to Y$, with no flatness assumption on $L$ and no Noetherian assumption on $R$. It does not assert that the unmodified base change of $\phi$ is itself an adequate moduli space.

The base change of $U$ along $T\to Y$ is $U_T=\operatorname{Spec}(E\otimes_RL)$. To check the identification with its projections, a map from an affine test scheme $\operatorname{Spec}B$ to this spectrum is a ring map $E\otimes_RL\to B$, equivalently ring maps $E\to B$ and $L\to B$ agreeing on $R$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] this is exactly a pair of maps to $U$ and $T$ over $Y$. The universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product] thus identifies the fibre product on affine tests; affine opens cover every test scheme, so the unique maps glue and give the asserted isomorphism. The map to $T$ is induced by $l\mapsto1\otimes l$.

The square with $U_T=U\times_YT$ and $\mathcal X_T=\mathcal X\times_YT$ is the base change of $\pi$ along $\mathcal X_T\to\mathcal X$: a map to $U\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X_T$ is precisely a map to $U$ together with a compatible map to $T$, so this fibre product is $U_T$. By the base-change assertion of [lem-sfb-flat-affine-action-stack-presentation], $p:|U_T|\to|\mathcal X_T|$ is open and surjective. Hence $h=g\circ p$ is surjective. For $V\subseteq|T|$, if $h^{-1}V$ is open then $p(h^{-1}V)=g^{-1}V$ is open, using surjectivity of $p$. Step 4 then makes $V$ open. Conversely continuity of $h$ makes $h^{-1}V$ open whenever $V$ is open. By step 5, $h$ is exactly $\operatorname{Spec}(E\otimes_RL)\to\operatorname{Spec}L$. As $L$ was arbitrary, this proves the stated universal submersiveness.
